doc.title: Cal Collins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 11, 1997

title: Playing Goodman's repertoire and knowing thousands of tunes
summary: Goodman mostly used small groups with familiar tunes; musicians carry thousands of tunes in memory.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Now in that kind of situation, did he have music for you?
So in addition to having to be a good player, with the right attitude to please Benny I guess, you had to know all the tunes.
And did you have an idea when you got on the stand, like what’s he going to call?

It really didn’t make too much difference. He would call tunes that I was very familiar with, I’d been listening to him for years. That’s what we all did really. We would just, we know how he played the tune and it was like that, it was real easy, it was real easy, like you’d been doing it all your life. Now the times that I was with him, about four years I’ll say, we probably never did any more than six big band things, you know the big band things, about a half a dozen of them. The rest of them were all very small, quartet, quintet, sextet and all that stuff. But with the big band things I had chord charts and everything that I could sort of read a little bit. But it was easy, there was nothing to it. We knew everything he did.
That’s the fascinating part about jazz sometimes, how are they doing that? And you have to have a pretty big collection of tunes in your memory I would say.

Oh, you do. I’ve had people that are into that, maybe professional gamblers or something, that would tell me and a bunch of musicians, that you have no idea how many tunes you know, you have no idea. It’s in the thousands, literally. And you’re not even aware of it. I know it’s got to be true because once in a while I’ll play a tune — somebody’ll call a tune or if I’m playing with a singer, that I know, that I haven’t played for years, but it’s right there. Yeah. It’s one of those things.
